title: Checks for the presence of a return None statement when None is the only possible return value.
summary: Python implicitly assumes return None if an explicit return value is omitted. Therefore, explicitly returning None is redundant and should be avoided when it is the only possible return value across all code paths in a given function. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-return and made it stable in v0.0.154.
message_templates: Do not explicitly `return None` in function if it is the only possible return value

title: Checks for the presence of a return statement with no explicit value, for functions that return non-None values elsewhere.
summary: Including a return statement with no explicit value can cause confusion when other return statements in the function return non-None values. Python implicitly assumes return None if no other return value is present. Adding an explicit return None can make the code more readable by clarifying intent. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-return and made it stable in v0.0.154.
message_templates: Do not implicitly `return None` in function able to return non-`None` value

title: Checks for missing explicit return statements at the end of functions that can return non-None values.
summary: The lack of an explicit return statement at the end of a function that can return non-None values can cause confusion. Python implicitly returns None if no other return value is present. Adding an explicit return None can make the code more readable by clarifying intent. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-return and made it stable in v0.0.154.
message_templates: Missing explicit `return` at the end of function able to return non-`None` value

title: Checks for variable assignments that immediately precede a return of the assigned variable.
summary: The variable assignment is not necessary, as the value can be returned directly. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-return and made it stable in v0.0.154.

title: Checks for else statements with a return statement in the preceding if block.
summary: The else statement is not needed as the return statement will always break out of the enclosing function. Removing the else will reduce nesting and make the code more readable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-return and made it stable in v0.0.154.

title: Checks for else statements with a raise statement in the preceding if block.
summary: The else statement is not needed as the raise statement will always break out of the current scope. Removing the else will reduce nesting and make the code more readable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-return and made it stable in v0.0.154.

title: Checks for else statements with a continue statement in the preceding if block.
summary: The else statement is not needed, as the continue statement will always continue onto the next iteration of a loop. Removing the else will reduce nesting and make the code more readable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-return and made it stable in v0.0.154.

title: Checks for else statements with a break statement in the preceding if block.
summary: The else statement is not needed, as the break statement will always break out of the loop. Removing the else will reduce nesting and make the code more readable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-return and made it stable in v0.0.154.

title: Check that cast is not redundant.
summary: If you use --warn-redundant-casts, mypy will generate an error if the source type of a cast is the same as the target type. mypy does not enable this error code by default. Use --enable-error-code redundant-cast to enable it.

title: Check that expression is redundant.
summary: If you use --enable-error-code redundant-expr, mypy generates an error if it thinks that an expression is redundant. mypy does not enable this error code by default. Use --enable-error-code redundant-expr to enable it.

title: Check that methods do not have redundant Self annotations.
summary: If a method uses the Self type in the return type or the type of a non-self argument, there is no need to annotate the self argument explicitly. Such annotations are allowed by 673 but are redundant. mypy does not enable this error code by default. Use --enable-error-code redundant-self to enable it.

title: Check that function returns a value.
summary: If a function has a non-None return type, mypy expects that the function always explicitly returns a value (or raises an exception). The function should not fall off the end of the function, since this is often a bug. mypy enables this error code by default.

title: Check that return value is compatible.
summary: Mypy checks that the returned value is compatible with the type signature of the function. mypy enables this error code by default.
